items.stem:
The diagram shows a regular octagon.
A square ABQP is drawn on the side AB of the octagon.

parts.t: Show that each interior angle of a regular octagon is 135°.
Find the value of x.
Explain why regular octagons do not tessellate.

sols: All eight angles are equal because the octagon is regular.
The angles at the point A are the octagon angle, the square angle and x°.
angles at a point add up to 360°
For a shape to tessellate, a whole number of its interior angles must fit round a point.
<sup>360</sup>⁄<sub>135</sub> = 2.67…, which is not a whole number.
Two octagons leave a gap of 90° and three would overlap, so regular octagons do not tessellate.
ms:
M1 for (8 − 2) × 180 (= 1080) or 360 ÷ 8 (= 45)
A1 for a complete correct method reaching 135 nfww

B1
oe, e.g. 135 does not divide exactly into 360, so a gap of 90° is left

items.stem: Marek says that he has drawn a regular polygon in which each interior angle is 155°.

parts.t: Explain why Marek must be wrong.

sols: If the interior angle were 155°, each exterior angle would be 180 − 155 = 25°.
The number of sides would be 360 ÷ 25 = 14.4
the exterior angles add up to 360°
14.4 is not a whole number, so no regular polygon has an interior angle of 155°.
the number of sides must be an integer
ms:
M1 for 180 − 155 = 25 and 360 ÷ 25 oe
A1 for 14.4 with a statement that this is not a whole number
alternative: 155n = 180(n − 2) gives n = 14.4

ms:

A1 for a statement that the angles at a point add to exactly 360° (no gaps or overlaps)
